title: Retention Bug and Isolation Sequencing
description: Diagnose and fix a broken power-domain wake-up with sequencing assertions and data checks: release isolation last, reset before restoring, and catch an early release at the moment it happens.

steps.title: Step 1: Run the Starter and Read the Failures
steps.instructions: Predict first: with the wake-up order ISO_OFF, PWR_ON, RESTORE, CLK_ON in `buggy_tb.sv`, which assertions fail, from which time, and which read returns the wrong value? Then compile `buggy_tb.sv` alone with `tb_top` as the top module and run it unchanged. Record the first failure of each assertion and the summary. Expected (hand trace): `a_iso_unless_on` and `a_no_x_into_top` fail from 355 ns, `READ SCRATCH: expected 0x00 observed 0xxx` at 485 ns, and `PASS=4 FAIL=15`. Explain why CTX still reads 0xA5.

steps.title: Step 2: Reorder the Wake-Up
steps.instructions: Move `pmu(ISO_OFF)` to the end of the `[WAKE]` block (PWR_ON, RESTORE, CLK_ON, ISO_OFF) and run again. Expected: the X leak during the wake-up is gone, but SCRATCH still reads X at 485 ns, and the summary is `PASS=4 FAIL=2`. Name the step that is still missing before you go on.

steps.title: Step 3: Write a_release_after_wake
steps.instructions: Replace the TODO in `pwr_seq_checker` with `a_release_after_wake`: when `cpu_iso_en` falls, `cpu_pwr_ack`, `cpu_clk_en`, `cpu_rst_n`, `reset_seen` and `restored` must all be 1. Report with `fail("a_release_after_wake", ...)`. Rerun the Step 2 order: the new assertion fails at 435 ns, at the release and before any traffic, and the summary is `PASS=4 FAIL=3`.

steps.title: Step 4: Add the Domain Reset
steps.instructions: Make the wake-up PWR_ON, RST, RESTORE, CLK_ON, ISO_OFF. Run it: CTX reads 0xa5 at 485 ns, SCRATCH reads 0x00 at 515 ns, no assertion fails, and the last line is `PASS=5 FAIL=0`. Compare your file with `solution_tb.sv`.

steps.title: Step 5: Break It and Predict
steps.instructions: Predict each result before you run it (README, Step 5): (a) restore before reset gives `a_release_after_wake` at 465 ns, `READ CTX: expected 0xa5 observed 0x00` at 485 ns and `PASS=4 FAIL=2`; (b) power off before isolation on the sleep path: which assertion fails first, and why does CTX still come back as 0xA5? (c) save after power-off: which assertion names the mistake, and what does CTX read after the wake-up? Write down your predictions for (b) and (c), run them, and compare with the README's "Check your predictions" block, which gives the expected failures and summaries.

steps.title: Step 6 (Optional): Move the Order into UVM
steps.instructions: Write your fixed sleep and wake-up orders as the body of `power_cycle_vseq` from E-PWR-1 Make It Work: two `run_pmu({...})` calls, with `HOLD` as the last action of the power-down call, as in `power_cycle_vseq`, after the bus traffic has finished. Explain in one sentence why quiescing the bus is free when the bus sequences run in series.
